The present invention provides a soft polyurethane foam molded article (1) that has a mounting surface (1A) and is obtained by foam-molding a foaming stock solution. The soft polyurethane foam molded article (1) includes a plurality of layered parts (11 and 12) that form layers in a vertical direction (Y) perpendicular to the mounting surface. A plurality of foaming cells included in each of the layered parts have a ratio of a size in a lateral direction (X) along the mounting surface with respect to a size in the vertical direction that becomes larger as the foaming cells become positioned closer to the side of the mounting surface (1A) in the vertical direction. At boundaries (C1 and A2) between the layered parts adjacent to each other in the vertical direction, the ratio of a foaming cell included in the layered part (11) on the side of the mounting surface is lower than the ratio of a foaming cell included in the layered part (12) on the side of a back surface (1B) opposite to the side of the mounting surface.

The invention provides a soft polyurethane foam molded article having a mounting surface and produced by foam-molding a foaming stock solution. The molded article is configured to include a plurality of layered parts arranged in a vertical direction that is perpendicular to the mounting surface.

In each of the layered parts, the foaming cells have a size ratio defined by the ratio of their lateral dimension to their vertical dimension. This lateral-to-vertical size ratio becomes larger in layered parts positioned closer to the mounting surface. In other words, the foaming cells are shaped such that their lateral elongation relative to their vertical height increases toward the mounting surface.

At the boundary between adjacent layered parts, however, the relationship of the foaming cell size ratio is reversed locally. Specifically, the foaming cell size ratio in the layered part located closer to the mounting surface is lower than the foaming cell size ratio in the layered part located closer to the back surface. As a result, the molded article has a layered internal cell structure in which the cell shape varies in the vertical direction while maintaining distinctive cell-ratio differences at the interfaces between neighboring layered parts.
outputs.L4:
A soft polyurethane foam molded article is produced by foam-molding a foaming stock solution so that the resulting foam has a layered internal structure. The molded article includes a mounting surface, which may be a surface used for attachment, support, installation, or contact with another member. Within the article, a plurality of foam layers are arranged in a direction perpendicular to this mounting surface. In other words, the foam is formed as multiple vertical layers extending successively from a side opposite the mounting surface toward the mounting surface.

The internal foam structure is characterized by the shapes of the foaming cells contained in each layer. These cells are evaluated using a cell-size ratio, defined as the ratio of a lateral cell size to a vertical cell size. The lateral cell size refers to the dimension of a cell in a direction generally parallel to the mounting surface, while the vertical cell size refers to the dimension of the cell in a direction generally perpendicular to the mounting surface. By comparing these two dimensions, the degree of elongation or flattening of the cells can be quantified.

In the molded article, the cell-size ratio generally increases as the position approaches the mounting surface. This means that cells located closer to the mounting surface tend to have a larger lateral dimension relative to their vertical dimension than cells located farther away. As a result, the foam structure gradually changes through the thickness of the article, producing a controlled variation in cell shape and orientation.

However, at boundaries between adjacent vertical layers, the cell-size ratio decreases locally. Thus, although the overall trend is for the cell-size ratio to increase toward the mounting surface, each interface between neighboring layers produces a distinct drop in the ratio. This repeated increase-and-drop pattern makes it possible to identify the layered structure within the foam and to control the mechanical and physical properties of the molded article more precisely.

By forming the soft polyurethane foam in this manner, the molded article can be provided with a designed internal cellular structure rather than a uniform random foam structure. The controlled distribution of cell shapes may improve characteristics such as cushioning performance, load distribution, impact absorption, vibration damping, durability, ventilation, or comfort, depending on the intended application. Consequently, the molded article can achieve enhanced performance while maintaining the softness and resilience typically required of polyurethane foam products.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in English, but it is also one of the most important. It is called the definite article, and its main purpose is to point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener can identify.

This simple word helps create clarity. It tells us that something is known, unique, or already mentioned. For example, “I saw a dog. The dog was barking.” In the second sentence, “the dog” refers to the same dog introduced earlier.

“The” is also used with unique things, such as “the sun,” “the moon,” and “the sky.” It can appear before superlatives, like “the best,” “the tallest,” or “the most beautiful.” Though it is short and often unnoticed, “the” gives structure and meaning to countless sentences.

In many ways, “the” shows how powerful small words can be. Without it, English would be less precise, less natural, and much harder to understand.

The article (10) includes a mounting surface (11) to be mounted to a support member and a back surface (12) opposite the mounting surface (11). In a thickness direction (Z) extending from the mounting surface (11) toward the back surface (12), the article (10) has a plurality of layered parts, including a mounting-side layer (21), an intermediate layer (22), and a back-side layer (23).

### Patent Specification Excerpt

#### Title  
Soft Polyurethane Foam Molded Article

#### Technical Field  
The present invention relates to a soft polyurethane foam molded article suitable for use as a cushioning member, a sound-absorbing member, an interior member, or a vibration-damping member, and particularly relates to a molded article having layered foam portions with controlled foam-cell size relationships in predetermined directions.

#### Summary  
A soft polyurethane foam molded article (1) comprises a first layered part (11) and a second layered part (12) laminated in a thickness direction between a mounting surface (1A) and a back surface (1B). The mounting surface (1A) is a surface configured to be mounted to, or brought into contact with, an opposing member, and the back surface (1B) is positioned on an opposite side of the molded article (1) from the mounting surface (1A).

In the molded article (1), a vertical direction is defined as a direction Y extending from the mounting surface (1A) toward the back surface (1B), and a lateral direction is defined as a direction X intersecting the vertical direction Y. Preferably, the lateral direction X is substantially orthogonal to the vertical direction Y.

The first layered part (11) is disposed closer to the mounting surface (1A) than the second layered part (12), and the second layered part (12) is disposed closer to the back surface (1B) than the first layered part (11). Each of the first layered part (11) and the second layered part (12) is formed of soft polyurethane foam having a plurality of foam cells.

#### Foam-Cell Size Relationships  
Let:

- \(D_{11Y}\) be an average foam-cell size of the first layered part (11) measured in the vertical direction Y;  
- \(D_{11X}\) be an average foam-cell size of the first layered part (11) measured in the lateral direction X;  
- \(D_{12Y}\) be an average foam-cell size of the second layered part (12) measured in the vertical direction Y; and  
- \(D_{12X}\) be an average foam-cell size of the second layered part (12) measured in the lateral direction X.

The soft polyurethane foam molded article (1) is configured so as to satisfy at least one, and preferably all, of the following relationships:

\[
1.05 \leq \frac{D_{11Y}}{D_{11X}} \leq 1.80
\]

\[
0.60 \leq \frac{D_{12Y}}{D_{12X}} \leq 0.95
\]

\[
1.10 \leq \frac{D_{11Y}}{D_{12Y}} \leq 2.50
\]

\[
0.70 \leq \frac{D_{11X}}{D_{12X}} \leq 1.30
\]

By satisfying the above relationships, the first layered part (11) has foam cells that are relatively elongated in the vertical direction Y, thereby improving compressive compliance and surface fitting performance at the mounting surface (1A). Meanwhile, the second layered part (12) has foam cells that are relatively enlarged in the lateral direction X, thereby improving shape retention, vibration absorption, and load distribution in the lateral direction X.

#### Detailed Description  
In one embodiment, the first layered part (11) and the second layered part (12) are integrally molded so that no distinct adhesive layer is present between the layered parts. The boundary between the first layered part (11) and the second layered part (12) may be a gradual transition region in which foam-cell size changes continuously in the vertical direction Y.

The mounting surface (1A) may be formed as a substantially flat surface, a curved surface, or a surface having projections, recesses, ribs, grooves, or other engagement structures. The back surface (1B) may be configured to face an interior space, an exterior panel, a support frame, or another structural member.

The foam-cell size may be determined from an enlarged cross-sectional image of the molded article (1). For example, a cross section parallel to the vertical direction Y and the lateral direction X may be observed, and the average foam-cell size in each direction may be calculated as an average Feret diameter of a plurality of cells. Preferably, the average foam-cell size is obtained from at least fifty foam cells in each layered part.

In a preferred embodiment, the molded article (1) satisfies:

\[
1.15 \leq \frac{D_{11Y}}{D_{11X}} \leq 1.50
\]

and

\[
0.70 \leq \frac{D_{12Y}}{D_{12X}} \leq 0.90
\]

Such configuration provides a balance between softness at the mounting surface (1A) and dimensional stability near the back surface (1B).

#### Example Claim  
1. A soft polyurethane foam molded article (1) comprising:  
   a mounting surface (1A);  
   a back surface (1B) opposite to the mounting surface (1A);  
   a first layered part (11) disposed closer to the mounting surface (1A); and  
   a second layered part (12) disposed closer to the back surface (1B),  
   wherein a vertical direction Y is defined from the mounting surface (1A) toward the back surface (1B), and a lateral direction X is defined to intersect the vertical direction Y,  
   wherein the first layered part (11) and the second layered part (12) are formed of soft polyurethane foam having foam cells, and  
   wherein, when average foam-cell sizes of the first layered part (11) in the vertical direction Y and the lateral direction X are respectively \(D_{11Y}\) and \(D_{11X}\), and average foam-cell sizes of the second layered part (12) in the vertical direction Y and the lateral direction X are respectively \(D_{12Y}\) and \(D_{12X}\), the following relationships are satisfied:

\[
1.05 \leq \frac{D_{11Y}}{D_{11X}} \leq 1.80
\]

and

\[
0.60 \leq \frac{D_{12Y}}{D_{12X}} \leq 0.95.
\]
